rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation is on line 109, changing `block_size * VEC_SIZE` to `block_size / VEC_SIZE` in the grid_size calculation for the float16 branch. Input specification mandates dtype=torch.float32, so execution always enters the float32 branch (line 94-102) which is UNCHANGED. The mutated float16 branch (line 103-112) is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation modifies the grid size calculation formula in the `torch::kFloat16` branch of the kernel launcher. Specifically, it changes `(size + block_size * VEC_SIZE - 1)` to `(size + block_size / VEC_SIZE - 1)`. However, the input specification explicitly requires `dtype=torch.float32`, which means the code always executes the `torch::kFloat32` branch starting at line 94. The float16 branch containing the mutation (starting at line 103) is completely unreachable for any float32 input. Since dtype is part of the fixed input specification and cannot be changed, no value-level modification can trigger the mutated code path. The Layer 2 testing confirmed bitwise equivalence across 112 test rounds because all tests used float32 tensors.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation resides exclusively in the float16 code path, but the input specification mandates float32 tensors. Changing the dtype would violate the testing contract. The only way to kill this mutant would be to change the input dtype to float16, which is not permitted.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should generate dtype-variant test cases when kernels have dtype-specific code paths. For this kernel, separate input specifications for float32 and float16 inputs would catch mutations in both branches. Additionally, dtype coverage analysis should flag when mutations exist in unreachable dtype branches.
